title: Split parts: lead and parts in one worktree

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
A split lets a large slice use a lead and parts with disjoint files, so parts can change different files at once. ork runs one implementer today and has no split run. The slicer contract puts the parts in the slice worktree (../slicer/src/slicer/ai.py:400), so this slice must not give each part its own worktree.

From S10 (carried here from S08): split-part and sliver prompts need the same 'no handoff before review' wording as the implementer prompt.

sections.body:

- `internal/engine/states.go` and `internal/engine/round.go` (implement and review rounds; parts run in one worktree).
- `internal/daemon/runs.go`:37,205 (Split param and RecommendRoles call).
- `internal/slicercli/types.go:171` (Split) and write.go:94 (--split).
- `internal/engine/*_test.go` (new split tests) and `internal/roles` tests.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- TestSplitPartsShareTheSliceWorktree: a lead and two parts run in one worktree.
- TestPartsRunInParallelOnlyWhenFilesAreDisjoint: overlapping parts run one after another (ai.py:400).
- TestPartRoundRunsNoSlicerWriteCommand: a part round records no slicer write (ai.py:334-336).
- TestSplitReviewSeesTheCombinedDiffOnce: one review and one gate cover the whole slice.
- TestSplitArchitectRunsOnlyOnSizeL: architect only on size L (design.md:191-193).
- The architect position follows record 123 (after accepted findings, before the gate): covered by S08.
